parole.significato: A traditional Welsh soup, typically made with beef, lamb, or salted bacon with carrot, leeks, potatoes, swedes, and oth…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Welsh cawl, itself borrowed from Latin caulis (“stalk or stem of a plant, particularly a cabbage”), from Proto-Indo-European *kaw(ǝ)l, *kh₂ulós, or *kowos (“tubular bone; pipe”). The English word is a doublet of caulis, cole, and kale.

parole.significato: A spiced mead, originally from Wales.
parole.testo: From metheglin, from Welsh meddyglyn, from meddyg (“medicinal”) (from Latin medicus) + llyn (“liquor”) (cognate with Irish lionn and Gaelic leann).

parole.significato: A spiced mead, originally from Wales.
parole.testo: From Welsh meddyglyn, from meddyg (“doctor, healer”) (from Latin medicus) + llyn (“liquor”) (cognate with Irish lionn and Gaelic leann).

parole.significato: A beverage composed of hot milk curdled by some strong infusion, such as wine.
parole.testo: From Middle English posset, possot, possate, poshet, posthot, of unclear origin. Perhaps from Welsh posel. A connection to Latin pōsca (medieval/dialectal poscada) has also been suggested.

parole.significato: An attic or loft, notably over a shippen.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Welsh taflod, from Middle Welsh taflawd, from Old Welsh *tablaut, borrowed from Latin tabulātum.

parole.significato: A saibling, a fish of species (Salvelinus alpinus).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Welsh torgoch (literally “red-belly”), from Latin coccum (“kermes berry, scarlet”), from Ancient Greek κόκκος (kókkos, “scarletberry”)
